The trunk tip is above the green pin: a red found after a landing took the pin back below the commit that caused it.
The trunk tip passed its landing gate and is not live yet: it goes live on the captain's word, or by itself in a batch when the project has a go-live waiver.
The captain said go live and the home has not moved yet. A project with a go-live waiver skips this state.
The home runs the trunk tip.
A red check pinned the home back to the last good commit.
The live hook failed, so the home stayed where it was.

column2: p=$1; [ -n "${JG_HOME:-}" ] || { echo no-jg-home; exit 0; }; s=$JG_HOME/state; rd() { cat "$s/$1-$p" 2>/dev/null; }; t=$(rd trunk-tip); g=$(rd trunk-green); r=$(rd trunk-released); w=$(cut -f1 "$s/trunk-word-live-$p" 2>/dev/null); l=$(awk -F'\t' -v p="$p" -v g="$g" '$1==p&&$2==g{x=$4} END{print x}' "$JG_HOME/data/trunk-live.tsv" 2>/dev/null); [ -n "$t" ] || exit 0; if [ "$t" = "$r" ]; then [ -e "$s/trunk-rolled-$p" ] && echo rolled || echo released; exit 0; fi; case $l in hook-failed) echo hook-failed;; live,pinned-behind*) echo pinned-behind;; live) [ "$t" = "$g" ] && echo live || echo landed;; *) if [ "$t" != "$g" ]; then echo landed; elif [ -n "$w" ] && [ "$w" = "$g" ]; then echo word-given; else echo green; fi;; esac
